Build a two_panel Leaflet map with optional climate panel and click_to_zoom

Source: R/custom_functions.r
fx.build.klima.map.Rd

This function constructs a two_panel HTML layout consisting of a large leaflet map on the left and an optional information panel on the right. The map always displays the supplied catchment polygon(s), together with Geocache WMAS WGS84 basemaps, provider tiles, and optional popup tables derived from climate mappings. If a klima table is supplied, it is rendered as a static HTML panel in the right_hand column.

Usage

fx.build.klima.map(
  s = NULL,
  map6190 = NULL,
  map9120 = NULL,
  klima = NULL,
  map.width = "1000%",
  map.height = "900px",
  station_name = "Station",
  station_lon = NULL,
  station_lat = NULL
)

Arguments

s

An sf object containing the catchment polygon(s) from NEVINA. Required. The geometry is automatically transformed to EPSG:4326 for Leaflet.

map6190

Optional named character vector mapping standardized climate variable names to shapefile fields for the 1961-1990 period. If provided together with map9120, popup tables will be generated.

map9120

Optional named character vector mapping standardized climate variable names to shapefile fields for the 1991-2020 period. Used together with map6190 to build popup tables.

klima

Optional data frame or matrix containing a combined climate summary table (wide format) with columns Variable, 1961-1990, and 1991-2020. If supplied, the table is displayed in a right_hand information panel.

map.width

Width of the Leaflet map widget default "100%"

map.height

Height of the Leaflet map widget (default "900px").

station_name

Character. Name of station (default "Station").

station_lon

Numeric. Longitude of station (default NULL).

station_lat

Numeric. Latitude of station (default NULL).

Value

A browsable HTML widget containing the two_panel layout. The left panel contains the Leaflet map; the right panel contains the optional climate table.

Details

A click_to_zoom feature is included: clicking the catchment polygon resets the map view to the full spatial extent of the shapefile. This is implemented via a small JavaScript handler attached through htmlwidgets::onRender().
